In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SP-D modulates allergen uptake in a complex epithelial airway cell model, which is associated with decreased secretion of inflammatory mediators.
SP-D is able to reduce the allergenicity of SPP by modulating their uptake in epithelial cells, as well as by modulating the inflammatory response of macrophages, dendritic cells, and T-lymphocytes.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SP-D can modulates the uptake of allergen particles by epithelial cells as well as by immune effector cells, thereby modulating the inflammatory response.
SP-D can act in a cell-type specific way to modulate the uptake of allergen particles as well as the inflammatory response in the lower airways.
SP-D modulates the uptake of allergen particles in the epithelial airways and thereby influences the inflammatory response.
The main takeaway from our work is that

SP-D is not only a passive barrier, which prevents allergens from entering the lower airways but that it also actively modulates the uptake of allergen particles by different cells and thereby modulates the secretion of pro- inflammatory cytokines.
SP-D can modiate the inflammatory response by influencing the uptake of allergen particles in a cell type dependent fashion.
SP-D is a potential candidate for the treatment of allergic asthma.
